title: We Automated the Review
cards: We added an AI reviewer to save developers time.
First pull request: three hundred suggestions.
And some were really good!
So the coding agent fixed them.
Three hundred fixes.
Then the reviewer reviewed the fixes.
More suggestions!
One agent renamed a function.
The other wanted a clearer name.
They discussed it all morning. Through commits!
Every commit started a pipeline.
Our tests run in ninety seconds.
We spent months optimizing them.
Ninety seconds!
After six hours waiting for a runner.
At nine, all the developers logged in.
Each one started five agents.
The runners were fully booked before stand-up.
So we doubled the runners.
The queue started moving!
The agents got feedback faster!
And immediately submitted more fixes.
We'd upgraded the traffic jam.
Then we added an autoscaler.
Finally, something could keep up with the agents.
The cloud bill.
And the human reviewers? Still there!
Someone has to check the AI's suggestions.
Now they read the code, the review, the fix...
And the review of the fix.
We automated everything except understanding it.
Finance asked us to reduce infrastructure costs.
No problem. The agent wrote a patch.
Beautiful patch. Turns off unnecessary runners.
Did we deploy it? Not yet.
It's waiting for a runner.
And the AI reviewer has a few suggestions.
